current.text: Julius Randle joined Brooklyn. Randle is ball-dominant and plays the same position, so Porter will play more at small forward.
Brooklyn's projected starters are Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Porter, Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe.
His usage was about 32% last season. Experts expect it to drop because Randle, Brown and Demin will all take more of the ball.
Josh Minott and Noah Clowney may also take some of his minutes.
He is an unrestricted free agent next summer and has no extension.

A trade is still very possible this season, mainly if he and the Nets do not agree on an extension. The Nets do not seem to see him as a long-term piece. Slater expects a trade within about six months.
Josh ranks him better than pick 60 if he stays in Brooklyn, and not far behind that even if he is traded.
Experts expect him to produce less than he did last season.
Josh ranks him 45 to 60 in category leagues. He calls him a fair mid-round price, and a round 6 pick is good value.
One expert says ESPN's rank of 42 is too high because Randle makes a repeat of last season hard to believe.
Another expert calls him undervalued on Yahoo and puts his worst case at around 75th.
The hamstring injury that ended his last season is not seen as a major concern for this season.
Houston controls Brooklyn's draft pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank. Experts say he may play more games than last season, when he sat out March.
March minutes are still uncertain. Brooklyn also has no team reason to win and may give second-half minutes to its young players.
He made 3.4 threes per game on 36.2%. That was the lowest percentage among the top six three-point makers, and his three-point volume may drop.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. Its playoff schedule with a March 28 end is 3-4-3 games, with only one back-to-back.
Brooklyn is projected to win about 28 games, with a range of roughly 22 to 30.

durable.text: He gives points, many threes and good rebounds. His value comes from efficiency and usage.
He gives little in assists, steals and blocks, and he does not get to the rim much.
He has a long injury history, including a hamstring injury late last season.
